newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ends evacuation of Iraq aid workers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ends evacuation of Iraq aid workers.

text.p: The State Department said on Monday it had completed the evacuation of nearly 4,000 employees of aid agencies from the Kurdish region of northern Iraq for settlement in the United States.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the last of the employees were taken from Iraq to Turkey last Friday and the last flight from Turkey arrived on Sunday on the Pacific island of Guam, a U.S. territory.
A total of 3,780 people were evacuated in an operation that began on Dec. 4.

The evacuees are being housed at Andersen Air Force Base on Guam, and will be considered for asylum in the United States, Burns said. U.S. officials have said in the past that most or all are expected to receive asylum.

Washington had already evacuated to Guam some 2,700 Iraqi aid workers directly employed by the U.S. government and Iraqi opposition figures in fear of Baghdad's recent increased influence in northern Iraq. U.S. officials say some of those have already reached the continental United States.
The latest evacuation involved employees of Western non-governmental organisations that were either U.S.-funded or U.S.-based.
The evacuations began after the Kurdistan Democratic Party invited Iraqi forces into the Western-protected Kurdish region at the end of August to help it fight a rival Kurdish faction.
